clue.text: A representative's within call where the accommodation's temporary

indicators.note: within says the representative piece sits inside the word for call

parts.note: to call someone, as to court, is to cite them
an MP is a representative in Parliament, so the possessive gives MP'S

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a delegate's lodging, close enough to shout to, is only a stopgap.
explanation.walkthrough: MP is a Member of Parliament, Britain's elected representative; with A it goes inside CITE, a summons.
explanation.definitionFit: A site for tents or caravans is a place where people stay only briefly.

clue.text: 7 allowed a heraldic device

parts.note: the answer to 7 down means angry, which is cross
let means allowed

explanation.surface: An angry knight is permitted a coat-of-arms emblem.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry this is a small cross whose arms are themselves crossed, a charge on a shield.

clue.text: An instrument for oil men and constructors

indicators.note: constructors are builders, so the letters are put together into a new form

explanation.surface: A kitchen tool for petroleum workers and builders.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of OIL MEN AND gives a variant spelling of the stringed instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variant of the lute-like stringed instrument with paired strings.

clue.text: Pay the little twister!

explanation.surface: A rallying cry to reward the small rogue.
explanation.definitionFit: Screw is slang for wages; it is also a small threaded fastener that is turned.

clue.text: Social crawler in a built-up area

definitions.text: Social crawler in a built-up area

parts.words: Social crawler in a built-up area
parts.note: an insect living in a colony inside a mound it builds itself, read as a creep in town

explanation.surface: A creep who socialises in town.
explanation.definitionFit: These colonial insects crawl and build tall earth mounds.

clue.text: Given little publicity — a bad habit for counsel

parts.note: an ad, short for advertisement, is a small piece of publicity
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: Keep it quiet: advice on a vice from someone who wants it hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: Counsel as a noun is guidance offered to someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Many is the way to hold forth

parts.note: D is 500 in Roman numerals, a large number
a course is a way or route

explanation.surface: Many say this is how to deliver a lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: D, the Roman numeral for 500, stands for 'many'.
explanation.definitionFit: To discourse is to speak at length on a subject, a synonym.

clue.text: The first person to deserve being put out

parts.note: I is the first-person pronoun
to rate is to deserve, as in rating a mention

explanation.surface: The front-runner merits being evicted.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone put out is annoyed or angry, a synonym.

clue.text: One and one don't make two!

definitions.text: One and one don't make two!

parts.words: One and one don't make two!
parts.note: written side by side, two ones form a two-digit number rather than their sum

explanation.surface: A protest at bad arithmetic.
explanation.definitionFit: The figures 1 and 1 placed together read as the number after ten.

clue.text: Various individuals going under

explanation.surface: Assorted people are sinking.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers is an old word for several or sundry; it is also the plural of one who swims underwater.

clue.text: Children wouldn't hold the proprietor back

indicators.note: back says the run of letters found there is read from right to left
the words Children wouldn't hold the letters running across them

explanation.surface: Youngsters refuse to restrain the shop owner as he retreats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hold' picks RENWO across 'childREN WOuldn't'; 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: A proprietor is the person who possesses a business or property, a synonym.

clue.text: Restore control by the body politic

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in keeping a rein on spending
the body politic is the organised nation, the state

explanation.surface: A call to give government back its grip on affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore someone is to put them back in a former position, a synonym.

clue.text: New show — it's been created for an animated heroine

indicators.note: something newly created is made up afresh, so these letters are built into a new order

parts.note: only the IT is fodder; the 's (is) belongs with the indicator

explanation.surface: A theatre announcement: a fresh production has been made around a cartoon heroine.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of NEW SHOW IT gives the Disney princess's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale princess is the heroine of a famous cartoon feature film, an example.

clue.text: Get direction on personal decoration if overweight

indicators.note: in an across answer on means the direction follows the decoration

parts.note: the OBE (Order of the British Empire) is an honour awarded to individuals
SE is south-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: A medal-wearer is told which way to go if too heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: The OBE is a British honour given to a person, worn as a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: Obese means very fat, well above a healthy weight, a synonym.

clue.text: Record first the French communication

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record
1st is the short form of first, here spelt with letters
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Logging a French message before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter, especially a formal or biblical one, is a written communication.

clue.text: Jaded feeling, of dissenter in confusion

indicators.note: in confusion says the letters of the word are muddled

explanation.surface: A rebel feels worn out by the chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Being jaded is being worn out, so the feeling is weariness.

clue.text: Secures vessel full of gin

indicators.note: full of says the ship's letters are filled with the word for gin

parts.note: SS is a steamship, a vessel
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: A ship loaded with spirits is made fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink but is the old word for a snare.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap something is to fasten it with a band, so it secures it.

clue.text: 21 ac is about the same for a top man

indicators.note: is about says the earlier answer goes round the same

parts.note: the answer to 21 across
id. is short for idem, Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A current affairs note: the boss is much the same.
explanation.walkthrough: ID is an abbreviation of Latin idem, 'the same', used in references.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a republic or organisation is its chief, a synonym.

clue.text: Colours — as usual

explanation.surface: The flag flies in its normal hues.
explanation.definitionFit: A regiment's colours are its flag; standard as an adjective also means normal.

clue.text: Private soldiers in a group

indicators.note: in says the soldiers are placed within the group

parts.note: a sect is a group, often religious
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Army privates are drafted into a unit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like a soldier's rank; it is the adjective meaning hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: Something private is kept confidential, a synonym.

clue.text: A Northerner rising in alarm

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word is read upwards, from the bottom

parts.note: a Scot is a person from Scotland, in the north of Britain

explanation.surface: A Scotsman getting up in a panic.
explanation.definitionFit: A tocsin is a bell rung as an alarm signal, a synonym.

clue.text: This time make a donation

explanation.surface: Now is the moment to give generously.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs on into 23 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The present is the current moment; to present is also to hand over a gift.

clue.text: Mean to grab share

parts.note: par is the average or norm, the mean
to take is to grab

explanation.surface: A miser sets out to seize a portion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like stingy; it is the average.
explanation.definitionFit: To partake is to have a share in something, a synonym.

clue.text: An ecclesiastic embraced by another is touched

indicators.note: embraced by says the cleric sits inside the other churchman

parts.note: a DD, Doctor of Divinity, is another churchman
an abbé is a French cleric

explanation.surface: One cleric being hugged by another is moved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touched' looks like moved; it means pressed lightly.
explanation.definitionFit: To dab is to touch lightly, so dabbed means touched.

clue.text: … though it may be a drawback

indicators.note: back read off the word drawback tells the solver to turn the word draw round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing 21: a gift can turn out to be a mixed blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' points back to the donation in 21 across. Read 'drawback' as 'draw back': A plus WARD, the word draw reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize or grant is a donation of the kind the pronoun refers to.

clue.text: Tired of wrestling?

explanation.surface: Is a grappler weary?
explanation.definitionFit: All-in means exhausted; all-in wrestling is a freestyle form of the sport.

clue.text: People going behind a vehicle could well be a bloomer

indicators.note: going behind says the people come after the vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Pedestrians trailing a car might well commit a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a mistake; it is a flower.
explanation.definitionFit: This pink flower is something that blooms, a playful sense.

clue.text: Pole writing article on poetry

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
an ode is a poem

explanation.surface: A Polish author's piece on verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a person from Poland; it is an electrode.
explanation.definitionFit: The positive electrode of a cell is one of its two terminals.

clue.text: Bear with an ill-disposed dancer

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so these letters are set out afresh

explanation.surface: A grumpy dancer has to put up with things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-disposed' splits: ILL is fodder with BEAR and AN, and 'disposed' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal female dancer in a ballet company is an example.

clue.text: Love for a particular kind of music

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: Someone loves one genre of music.
explanation.definitionFit: Sung drama with orchestra is a specific musical form, an example.

clue.text: A girl's need is for change

indicators.note: for change says these letters are swapped into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A young woman needs some small coins.
explanation.definitionFit: Denise is a female given name.

clue.text: Frustrated achievement indeed!

indicators.note: indeed is read as in deed, so the achievement goes inside the second part

parts.note: taken as written
a feat is an achievement

explanation.surface: A sarcastic 'what an achievement!'
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'indeed' as 'in deed': FEAT goes inside DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being beaten means having one's plans thwarted, a synonym.
